Lessons.Title: Quadratic Functions
ExplanationParagraphs: Original source objectives: identify a parabola’s axis, vertex and intercepts; convert general and vertex forms; determine domain/range and maxima/minima; find complex and real roots; model constrained quadratic optimization.
A quadratic f(x)=ax²+bx+c (a≠0) has axis x=−b/(2a). Writing f(x)=a(x−h)²+k exposes vertex (h,k) and its maximum or minimum.
For intercepts set x=0 for y and set f(x)=0 for x. The discriminant Δ=b²−4ac determines real intersections versus complex conjugate solutions.
The vertex controls range and optimizes a maximum area, revenue or height when its x-value lies in the physical model’s admissible domain.
For projectile formulas, report both algebraic roots but reject negative physical time and state units.
Independent Edulytics Cool-down: (a) Rewrite 2x²−12x+11 in vertex form. (b) Find real/complex roots of x²+4=0. (c) Maximize R(p)=−3p²+90p under p≥0.
Independent Try It 1 — Vertex from graph. A parabola has vertex (1,−3) and passes through (2,−1). Find its equation.
Independent Try It 2 — Complete square. Rewrite x²−4x+7 in vertex form.
Independent Try It 3 — Domain and range. Determine range of −2(x+3)²+5.
Independent Try It 4 — Solve real and complex roots. Find roots of 2x²−4x+5.
Independent Try It 5 — Projectile optimization. h(t)=−16t²+96t+112. Find peak time and height; positive impact time.

KeyConcepts.Title: Quadratic domain/range
KeyConcepts.Definition: Unrestricted quadratic has domain R and vertex-controlled range.

KeyConcepts.Title: Zeros and discriminant
KeyConcepts.Rule: Positive Δ two distinct real, zero double real, negative two nonreal conjugates.

KeyConcepts.Title: Quadratic formula
KeyConcepts.Rule: Preserve exact radicals and complex solutions.

KeyConcepts.Title: Graph intercepts
KeyConcepts.Rule: A parabola may have 0,1,2 real horizontal intersections.

KeyConcepts.Title: Optimization by vertex
KeyConcepts.Definition: A quadratic model with negative leading coefficient peaks at its vertex.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Verify physical input domain before optimizing.

KeyConcepts.Title: Transformation
KeyConcepts.Definition: a scales/reflections; h shifts horizontal; k shifts vertical.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use vertex form to read transformed y=x².

KeyConcepts.Title: Contextual domains
KeyConcepts.Definition: Time/distance/production may be nonnegative and bounded.

SummaryPoints: The quadratic vertex form is a(x−h)²+k.
Sign of a determines opening; vertex value determines range.
Discriminant determines real versus complex zeros.
Contextual optimization must observe admissible inputs.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The sign of the linear coefficient must be reversed.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Claiming negative discriminant means no solutions.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It means no real roots, but there are complex solutions.
The mathematical vertex can be outside permissible time or quantity.
